L2t: The word genome was coined in the 1920s by combining 'gene' and 'chromosome', and it is used across all kinds of organisms from viruses to humans.
L3t: A genome is the complete set of genetic material carried by an organism, so it includes every chromosome (plus any extra-chromosomal DNA such as mitochondrial DNA), not just one piece.
L4t: The genome is the entire DNA sequence of an organism, covering all of its chromosomes and other DNA.
L2f: The term genome was introduced in the 1990s alongside the Human Genome Project and applies only to complex multicellular organisms.
L3f: Each chromosome is a self-contained unit of heredity that carries a full genetic blueprint, so the genome is defined at the level of a single chromosome.
L4f: The genome is the DNA sequence of an entire chromosome.
cand_true: the entire DNA sequence of an organism
cand_wrong1: the DNA sequence of an entire chromosome
cand_wrong2: the set of all proteins an organism produces
